paragraphs: Mah sheomerim veatta atid littela veku' hakkavvana hu kemo shekkatab rabbenu za"l beseper "peri etz chayyim" dap t' ki middat hammalkut notelet nishmot yisrael ballayla beet hashshena umachazeret otam babboqer besod "chodashim labbeqarim" (iyyob g, kg) vedabar zeh hu toba gedola lanneshama kannoda velaken kaasher meqitz haadam modeh umeshabbeach al hattoba hazzot asher yassig ballayla habbaa, vehu modeh al heatid veomer veatta atid littelah mimmenni ballayla dehaynu shettaaleh hanneshama besod miyyayin nuqbin el malkut, ulehachazirah bi babboqer besod "chadashim labbeqarim", ukemo shekkatab beseper hakkavvanot od bedabar zeh bidrushe hallayla dap "z ammud d', besod happasuq hazzeh shel "chadashim labbeqarim" dinshamot hattachtonim olim bekol layla lahekol ulehitabber betok hammalkut veachar kak babboqer yotzeot mishsham mechuddashot ayyen sham, veken meporash gam ken bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l beshaar maamre rashbi"y bebeur iddera zuta dap n" shekkatab sham vezeh leshono bekol layla velayla olin neshamot hattachtonim besod "beyadeka apqid ruchi" (tehillim l, v) beet hashshekiba umitabberet mehem hammalkut haelyona besod "chadashim labbeqarim rabba emunateka", vetoelet aleha hahi inyanah hu kede lechaddesh et hanneshamot hahem velatet koach bahem ulehair bahem ukeinyan hachiddush hazzeh hu mah shemmechaddesh umetaqqen hammochin shel haadam shehu bechinat hanneshama shel hayyoshebet bammocha kannoda ad kan leshono hare nitbaer leka inyan zeh heteb: veda deap al pi shekkatab rabbenu zikrono libraka lechayye haolam habba sham dinshamot hattachtonim en yekolin laalot besod miyyayin nuqbin ballayla kannizkar leel ella ad sheyyihyeh ben y"g shana veyom echad abal bepachot mikkak en shum neshama yekola laalot besod min nuqbin kelal veim ken lepi zeh yesh lehaqshot ek haqqetannim min y"g shana omerim hodaa zo debirkat hashshachar hannizkarot dela shayeka bahem, hinneh al zeh yesh lomar diqtannim kevan deniklalim bigdolim yekolim lebarek beraka zo, veqarob lazeh ita bedibre rabbotenu za"l sheyyukal adam lebarek birkat hashshachar ap al pi shello nitchayyeb bahem deal minhago shel olam nitqenu, veap al gab debibraka zo hu modeh al atzmo veeno omer bilshon nistar, ha ikka berakot dimbarek al atzmo veap al gab dela hava beh kegon birkot hammaabir ap al gab dela yashan kelal, veken birkat sheasa li kol tzarekki beabel, vehu haddin gabbe beraka shel haqqetannim: venachazor leinyan rishon lebaer od mah sheomari hodaa ubilshon atid veen omerim bilshon abar, demin harauy sheyyitten haadam hodaa al heabar meh asa hqb"h chesed immo ballayla hazzo shel oto hayyom sheomed bo atta beummedu mishshinto shehechezir elayv nishmato vechiddesh otah bammocha shello, hinneh beemet nitqena hodaa zo bilshon atid kede liklol bah od kavvana acheret vehu ki leatid labo gam ken yihyeh kazot shettiqqach hammalkut et nishmot hatztzaddiqim besod miyyayin nuqbin veyachzeru lehitchaddesh bishlemut hamulleh meod sheen kamohu, velaken nosap behodaa zo milot ellu shel leatid labo dehaya day lomar littelah mimmenni ulehachazirah bi, ak hosip milot leatid labo kede liklol bah hakkavvana hashshenit hannizkeret sheanachnu mekavvenim behodaatenu zo lehodot lehashshem yitbarek gam al hattoba hannisgaba asher yaaseh lanu leatid labo hi dugmat hattoba hazzot sheoseh ittanu bazzeman hazzeh bekol layla veyom, veayyen beseper "peri etz chayyim" shekkatab bebeur beraka zo vezeh leshono vegam leatid yihyeh ken ayyen sham, veken besiddur rabbenu harasha"sh za"l katub kak atid littela mimmenni lemayyen nuqbin ulehachazirah bi bekol boqer vegam leatid labo ad kan ayyen sham:

clarification.explanation:
Regarding what is said in the blessing 'Elohai Neshamah,' 'You are destined to take it from me' — the intention (based on Peri Etz Chayim): the attribute of Malkhut takes the souls of Israel at night during sleep and returns them in the morning, in the secret of 'new every morning,' and this is a great benefit for the soul — for it ascends in the secret of mayin nukvin (feminine waters) to Malkhut, is renewed there, and emerges in the morning renewed and illuminated (so too in Sha'ar Ma'amarei Rashbi, Idra Zuta). Therefore when a person awakens he gives thanks for this benefit — and in future tense, for what he will merit on the coming night.
And although the Ari wrote that souls cannot ascend in the secret of mayin nukvin except from the age of thirteen years and one day — one might ask, how then do minors recite this thanksgiving? Rather, minors, since they are included within adults, may recite it; and further, a person may recite the morning blessings even though he was not obligated in them, for they were instituted 'according to the custom of the world' (like 'HaMaavir sheinah,' recited even by one who did not sleep, and 'she'asah li kol tzorki' recited by a mourner).
And the reason it is said in future tense and not past tense (although it would be fitting to give thanks for the kindness of the previous night) — is to include an additional intention: that in the future to come, Malkhut will take the souls of the righteous in the secret of mayin nukvin and they will return to be renewed in supreme perfection beyond compare; therefore 'le'atid lavo' (in the future to come) was added, to thank God also for the exalted good He will do for us in the future, similar to that done every night (so too in the siddur of the Rashash).
takeaways: 'You are destined to take it' — Malkhut takes the soul at night (mayin nukvin) and returns it renewed in the morning ('new every morning'), and this is a great benefit.

Minors recite this even though according to the secret this ascent applies only from age 13 — because they are included within adults, and because the morning blessings were instituted according to the custom of the world.
It is said in future tense — to include also a thanksgiving for the exalted good that will be given to the righteous in the future to come.

paragraphs: Yismok beraka zo shel elohay veku' lebirkat asher yatzar, ki beraka zo tzerika lihyot semuka lachabertah veyesh sod baddabar nizkar beshaar hakkavvanot, vetzarik lehapsiq meat ben tebat elohay letebat neshama kede shello yuban shehanneshama hi elohayv chas veshalom, veen lomar tehora hi ella yomar tehora, atta beraata vekannizkar kol zeh baacharonim, umah shechotem lipgarim metim kak niqraim haggupim habbetelim mimmelaaktam veshobetin mittenuatam, depigger leshon bittul hu kemo "asher piggeru meabor" (shemuel- l, y), veken bilshon chakamenu za"l depigre rabbanan, umah sheomerim metim dehashshena echad mishshishshim mimmita vehu siman litchiyyat hammetim leatid vekannizkar besiddur rab yabetz za"l: veda ki bibraka zo yesh shiba vearbaim tebot keminyan hvy"h hy"h kemo shekkatab rabbenu harasha"sh za"l, velaken lo yomar shette tebot sheatta hu qodem ribbon kol hammaasim, kakkatub bassiddurim ella yomar velohe abotay ribbon kol hammaasim:

clarification.explanation: The blessing 'Elohai Neshamah' should be juxtaposed to the blessing 'Asher Yatzar' (there is a secret in this). One should pause slightly between 'Elohai' and 'Neshamah' (so that it not be understood, God forbid, that the soul is his god). One does not say 'tehorah hi' (it is pure), but rather 'tehorah, atah bera'atah' (pure — You created it). 'Pegarim meitim' (dead corpses) — the body idle from labor during sleep (from the language of 'cessation'). The comparison of sleep to death (one-sixtieth of death) is a sign for the future resurrection of the dead. The blessing contains forty-seven words (corresponding to the numerical value of Havayah and Ehyeh); and one says 've'Elohei avotai Ribon kol hama'asim' (not 'she'atah hu... kodem Ribon').
takeaways: The blessing 'Elohai Neshamah': pause between 'Elohai' and 'Neshamah'; say 'tehorah, atah bera'atah' (not 'tehorah hi'), and 've'Elohei avotai Ribon kol hama'asim.'

paragraphs: Yizzaher lekavven bibraka behazkarat shem havaya"h shemmazkiro beshem adonay sheyyetzayyer bachashabattu otiyyot shem havaya"h ubetok ot he" acharona yetzayyer shem dn"y, vegam yetzayyer beshem hashshillub shel hvy"h dn"y, umah tob umah naim lehizzaher bazeh bekol paam shemmazkir hashshem hen bipsuqim hen battepilla, vegam tzarik lehizzaher kesheyyazkir shem havaya"h yetzayyer bemachshabto otiyyot hashshem binquddot, ubassiddurim vechummashim nahagu lenaqqedo beniqqud "leolam", vekol hammitpallel velomed miqraot mittok hasseper az yihyeh zeh etzlo benaqel belo torach, veyizzaher shello yatchil lomar baruk ad sheyyachshebu belibbo veyeda al mah mebarek vekannizkar baacharonim za"l:

clarification.explanation: When mentioning the Name Havayah (which is read as 'Adonai'), one should picture in thought the letters of the Name Havayah, and within the final Hei picture the Name Adonai (the combination of the two Names) — at every mention, in verses and in prayer. One should also picture the vocalization (as it is customarily vocalized as 'le'olam' in the siddurim) — therefore one who studies from a book does this easily. One should not begin to say 'Baruch' before he knows in his thought for what he is blessing.
takeaways: When mentioning God's Name, one should picture in thought the letters of the Name (Havayah combined with Adonai) and its vocalization.
One should not begin to bless before knowing well for what one is blessing.

paragraphs: Birkat hannoten lassekvi bina lepi peshuta sekvi hu hattarnegol hayyodea bina zo lehabchin ben yom uben layela, rotzeh lomar ben emtza hayyom leemtza hallayla deim lo ken may ulmeh al shear baale chayyim vekannizkar b"shalme tzibbur", ak kepi dibre rabbenu haari"y za"l beshaar hakkavvanot sekvi hu sod haggebura shenniqra sekvi ubachatzi hallayla nimsheket hearat habbina al haggebura veaz hi mitmatteqet veyadua ki lel niqra qodem chatzot velayla achar chatzot, al ken mebarekin beraka zo achar chatzot layla veelak ayyen sham, ubakkavvanot rabbenu harasha"sh za"l siyyem lehabchin ben middat yom shehu sod haddekora hanniqra middat yom, sheatta matchil zeman tiqqunam shehu mechatzot hallayla ad chatzi hayyom, uben middat layla shehi hannuqba hanniqret middat layla shekkebar nishlam tiqqunam shehu mechatzot hayyom ad chatzi hallayla ad ken ayyen sham. vehaddabar barur degam hacheresh sheeno shomea kelal mebarek beraka zo veayyen "minchat aharon" kelal Adonai ot y"b:

clarification.explanation: The blessing 'HaNotein LaSechvi Binah' — according to the plain meaning, 'sechvi' is the rooster that distinguishes between day and night (otherwise what advantage would it have over other animals?). According to the Ari, 'sechvi' is the secret of the attribute of Gevurah, and from it the illumination of Binah is drawn at midnight and sweetens it — therefore this blessing is recited only after midnight. And our teacher the Rashash added a further reason for the distinction between before midnight and after: one must distinguish between the 'attribute of day,' which is the secret of the male, whose time of repair begins specifically from midnight until midday, and the 'attribute of night,' which is the secret of the female, whose repair is already completed from midday until midnight — and since the repair of the day only begins at midnight, this is the proper time to bless on the distinction between the two. Even a deaf person who does not hear at all recites this blessing.
takeaways: The blessing 'HaNotein LaSechvi Binah' is recited only after midnight (based on the secret, the sweetening of Gevurah by the illumination of Binah).

According to the Rashash: from midnight the repair of the 'attribute of day' (the male) begins, while the 'attribute of night' (the female) had already completed its repair beforehand — and this is why this is the proper time for the blessing.
A deaf person also recites this blessing.

paragraphs: Birkat poqeach ivrim hodaa lechasdo yitbarak deene haadam hayu segurot usetumot beshena ukeshenneor nipqechu enayv, vehinneh besuma ikka pelugetta bapposeqim im yebarek beraka zo o lav, vehaggaon chida" b"shiyyure beraka" hiskim denaqetinan lebarek, veken katab harab hammaggihha b"shalme tzibbur" ayyen sham, ubeemet ap al gab deqayma lan sapeq berakot lehaqel, beha naqetinan lebarek, mishshum dilpi daat rabbenu haari"y za"l beshaar hakkavvanot dekol berakot ellu al minhago shel olam nitqenu veap al pi shello nitchayyeb bahem haadam tzarik lebarek, im ken hu haddin besuma detzarik lebarek, ukeneged sebarat rabbenu haari"y za"l en lomar sapeq berakot lehaqel, veayyen mah shekkatabnu leqamman bebirkat sheasa li kol tzarekki:

clarification.explanation: The blessing 'Pokei'ach Ivrim' — thanksgiving for the opening of the eyes from sleep. There is a dispute whether a blind person recites it; the halachah is — he blesses (according to the opinion of the Ari that these blessings were instituted according to the custom of the world, and not only for one who is personally obligated in them).
takeaways: A blind person recites 'Pokei'ach Ivrim' even though he does not personally benefit, because the blessing was instituted according to the custom of the world.

paragraphs: Im berak zoqep kepupim qodem mattir asurim lo yebarek mattir asurim, mishshum dekaput qasheh meissur, vekevan deberak zoqep hare biklal matayim maneh, mihu tob lebarek mattir asurim beli shem umalkut ella yeharher shem umalkut bilbabo kede shello yechsar lo mispar haorot haromezim berakot ellu alehem, veod ha ikka rsh"l vb"ch depasequ lebarek, laken latzet yede chobat kulle alema yebarek belo shem umalkut veraq yeharher shem umalkut betok habberaka, vaapillu adam kaput belav haki mechamat choli sheeno yakol lazuz mimmittato, gam ken mebarek beraka zo deal minhago shel olam nitqenu berakot ellu veayyen minchat aharon kelal Adonai ot y"d:

clarification.explanation: If one recited 'Zokef Kefufim' before 'Matir Assurim' (out of order) — he should not recite 'Matir Assurim' again (since being bent is more severe than being bound, and it is already included). Nevertheless, it is good to recite 'Matir Assurim' without the Name and Kingship (and meditate upon them in his heart), in order to satisfy all opinions. Even a person confined to bed due to illness recites this blessing (according to the custom of the world).
takeaways: If one erred in the order of blessings (Zokef before Matir) — he completes 'Matir Assurim' without the Name and Kingship, meditating on them.

paragraphs: Im beshaa sheamar baruk atta Adonai hayeta kavvanato lebarek zoqep kepupim yesayyem zoqep kepupim, ap al gab deaz lo yukal lebarek mattir asurim ken katab harab "chayye adam" kelal ch' ot Adonai yeuyyan sham, ubesipri haq' "mqbtzyl" haaleti deen lismok alayv bazeh leabbed habberaka hashshenit veraq lekattechilla vadday tzarik lehizzaher shello yomar baruk atta Adonai ella al siyyum habberaka haiqqarit shetztzarik lebarek otah bedato behazkarat hashshem:

clarification.explanation: If at the beginning of 'Baruch Atah Hashem' one intended 'Zokef Kefufim,' he should conclude accordingly (even though he will then be unable to bless 'Matir Assurim' separately) — but one should not rely on this and lose a blessing; ab initio one must be careful that the intention at the mentioning of the Name be for the conclusion of the correct blessing from the outset.
takeaways: One must have in mind in advance which blessing he is reciting before saying 'Baruch Atah Hashem,' so as not to lose a blessing.

paragraphs: Achar malbish arumim yebarek hannoten layyaep koach ushette berakot ellu nitqenu al malbushe hannepesh sheyyesh adam meabbed lebush napsho legamre vehaqqadosh baruk hu bechasdo noten lah lebush chadash ki aruma hi veyesh eno chote kol kak leabbed hallebush legamre ella raq machalisho vehaqqadosh baruk hu bechasdo noten lo koach lechazzeqo bekol yom kaasher machazir lo nishmato babboqer:

clarification.explanation: After 'Malbish Arumim' one blesses 'HaNotein LaYa'ef Koach' — these two blessings relate to 'the garments of the soul': one who loses the garment of his soul entirely receives, by God's kindness, a new garment; one who only weakens it receives renewed strength every morning.
takeaways: 'Malbish Arumim' and 'HaNotein LaYa'ef Koach' relate to the 'garment of the soul,' which is renewed/strengthened every morning.

paragraphs: Birkat sheasa li kol tzarekki tiqqenuha al neilat minalim dehayyachep eno yakol laasot tzerakayv vetzareke beto vekevan delabesh minalayv keillu naasu lo kol tzerakayv deaz hu mukan laleket lekol asher yirtzeh vekannizkar b"shalme tzibbur" vekatab rabbenu za"l beshaar hakkavvanot dap b' ammud d "kol hch"y berakot sheyyesh min al netilat yadayim ad sop birkat hattora chayyab adam lesadderam ulebarekam bekol yom ap al pi shello nitchayyeb hu bahem lepi shekkullam hem remazim niplaim al orot elyonim veen lebattelam apillu im haadam lo yashan ballayla o im lo hesir mitznapto o begadayv o sudaro o minalayv vekayyotze bazeh tzarik lebarekan bekol yom kullan ap al pi shello nitchayyeb bahem lepi sheal minhago shel olam nitqenu chutz mibbirkat sheasa li kol tzarekki beyom tisha beab ubeyom hakkippurim sheaz kol haolam yechepim vegam chutz mibbirkat al netilat yadayim vaasher yatzar dishtayim ellu im lo nitchayyeb bahen en lebarek alehem" ad kan leshono, mukach lehedya middebarayv dehaabel yebarek sheasa li kol tzarekki meachar dekol haolam lobeshim minalim veraq betisha beab veyom hakkippurim ap al pi decholeh vechayya lobeshim bateli bemiutayhu veen kol haolam yekolim limshok orot bibraka zo baabur deellu hammeutim lobeshim minalim veken b"shalme tzibbur" hikricha middibre rabbenu za"l deabel mebarek yeuyyan sham amenam harab hechasid mhr" shrb"y za"l beseper "dibre shalom" dap s"d peresh kavvanot rabbenu za"l debae sheyyihyeh oto adam neheneh al kol panim beoto dabar shehu mebarek alayv velaken paseq vetane deabel lo yebarek kevan deeno neheneh ubesipri Adonai "mqbtzyl" hebeti debarayv veyishshabti diqduq dibre rabbenu za"l al nakon upiqpaqti bedibre harab "dibre shalom" hannizkar vetaanti alayv degam lepi habanato hinneh haabel gam ken neheneh mizzeh daacherim lobeshin minalim veosin lo tzerakayv mah sheen ken im yihyu yechepim veken hassuma mebarek poqeach ivrim mippene shenneheneh mippetichat enayim shel acherim vehaaleti iqqar dehaabel mebarek veken amma debar:

clarification.explanation: The blessing 'She'asah Li Kol Tzorki' was instituted regarding putting on shoes — for one who is barefoot cannot attend to his needs, and since he put on his shoes it is as if all his needs were met (ready to go wherever he wishes) (Shalmei Tzibbur). The Ari (Sha'ar HaKavanot) wrote that all eighteen blessings from 'Al Netilat Yadayim' until the end of the blessing of the Torah must be arranged and recited every day, even though one was not obligated in them, for they are all wondrous allusions to supernal lights and must not be omitted — even if one did not sleep, did not remove his garments/shoes, etc. — for they were instituted according to the custom of the world; except for 'She'asah Li Kol Tzorki' on the Ninth of Av and Yom Kippur (when everyone is barefoot), and except for 'Al Netilat Yadayim' and 'Asher Yatzar' (which, if one was not obligated in them, should not be blessed). It is proven that a mourner blesses 'She'asah Li Kol Tzorki,' since the entire world wears shoes (and only on the Ninth of Av and Yom Kippur are the sick and women in childbirth, who wear shoes, a negligible minority, unable to sustain the blessing for everyone). However, Rabbi Sharabi ('Divrei Shalom') explained that the Ari requires that the one blessing actually benefit from the matter, and therefore ruled that a mourner does not bless, since he does not benefit; but the Ben Ish Chai ('Makbetzi'el') disagreed, holding that the mourner too benefits — since others wear shoes and attend to his needs (unlike if they were barefoot) — just as a blind person blesses 'Pokei'ach Ivrim' because he benefits from others' sight — and concluded that the essential ruling is that a mourner blesses, and so the people practice.
takeaways: 'She'asah Li Kol Tzorki' was instituted regarding putting on shoes; one recites all the morning blessings every day even though not obligated (according to 'the custom of the world').
Exceptions: 'She'asah Li Kol Tzorki' on the Ninth of Av and Yom Kippur, and 'Al Netilat Yadayim' and 'Asher Yatzar' (only if obligated).
A mourner recites 'She'asah Li Kol Tzorki' (since he benefits from others attending to his needs) — and so is the practical ruling.

paragraphs: Ap al gab deheelu haacharonim im berak shello asani ishsha lo yebarek al goy veebed, veken im berak al ebed lo yebarek al goy im kol zeh yebarek beli shem umalkut viharher shem umalkut betok habberaka, vehannashim yebareku sheasani kirtzono beli shem umalkut deikka pelugta bazeh vesapeq berakot lehaqel vetob leharher shem umalkut betok habberaka:

clarification.explanation: One who blessed 'she'lo asani ishah' should not bless 'she'lo asani eved' and 'she'lo asani goy'; and one who blessed 'she'lo asani eved' should not bless 'she'lo asani goy.' The exemption runs in one direction only: 'she'lo asani goy' does not exempt the other two. Nevertheless, one recites them without the Name and Kingship and meditates upon the Name and Kingship in his heart. Women bless 'she'asani kirtzono' without the Name and Kingship (there being a dispute, and doubt regarding blessings is resolved leniently).
takeaways: 'She'lo asani ishah' exempts [the need for] 'eved' and 'goy,' and 'she'lo asani eved' exempts 'goy' — but not the reverse, and 'she'lo asani goy' exempts nothing; women bless 'she'asani kirtzono' without the Name and Kingship.

paragraphs: Birkat hammaabir mistayyemet bebaruk gomel chasadim tobim veku' velaken en onin amen achar utenuma meapape vetzarik lomar vayhi ratzon beva"v gam yomar hammaabir veku' bilshon yachid sheomer meene umeapape veken targileni tadbiqeni veken hashshear benosach vayhi ratzon veku' deken hu nuschat rabbotenu za"l bashsha"s veken hu besiddur rabbenu harasha"sh za"l veayyen "dibre shalom" dap s"h mah shekkatab bazeh yeuyyan sham:

clarification.explanation: The blessing 'HaMaavir Sheinah Mei'einai' concludes with 'Baruch Gomel Chasadim Tovim Le'amo Yisrael'; one does not answer Amen after 'u'tenumah mei'af'apai' (which is not the end of the blessing). One must say 'Vayehi Ratzon' (with a vav) in the singular ('mei'einai,' 'me'af'apai,' 'targileini,' 'tadbikeini') following the version of our Sages.
takeaways: The blessing 'HaMaavir Sheinah' is recited in the singular through the end of 'Vayehi Ratzon'; one does not answer Amen in the middle (only at the end).

paragraphs: Ap al pi detzarik lomar vehaareb beva"v im kol zeh shette berakot hen veonim amen achar beraka harishona veqodem vehaareb lo yilmod lo battora shebbiktab velo battora shebbeal peh bilti birkat hattora velipsoq din belo taam shari abal im yomar taam asur veken liktob dibre tora o lishmoa name asur belo birkat hattora abal hirhur muttar veyesh omerim ha dehirhur muttar haynu im yeharher belibbo bilbad bilti iyyun basseper. venashim name mebarekim birkat hattora veim yashan bayyom al mittato shinat qeba ikka pelugta i chashiba hepseq vetzarik lebarek o lav umishshum desapeq berakot lehaqel yebarek beli shem umalkut viharher shem umalkut belibbo umi shechatapattu shena betok birkot hashshachar az kol beraka shehu mesuppaq bah im berak o lav lo yebarek missapeq, vaapillu im hu mesuppaq bebirkat hattora veal kol panim yebarek beli shem umalkut viharher shem umalkut betok habberaka, veim shakach velo berak birkot hashshachar qodem tepilla yebarek achar hattepilla chutz mibbirkat hammachazir neshamot deniptar bebirkat mechayyeh hammetim, vechutz mibbirkat hattora shenniptar beahabat olam:

clarification.explanation: Although one says 've'ha'arev' with a vav — it is nevertheless two blessings, and one answers Amen after the first, before 've'ha'arev.' And before the blessing of the Torah one may not study Written or Oral Torah; to rule on a matter of law without stating the reason is permitted, but to state the reason is forbidden; likewise to write words of Torah or to hear them is forbidden without the blessing of the Torah — but mere contemplation is permitted (and some say this permission applies only if he contemplates in his heart alone, without looking into a book). Women too recite the blessing of the Torah. And if one slept a fixed sleep during the day on his bed — there is a dispute whether this constitutes an interruption requiring him to bless again; and since doubt regarding blessings is resolved leniently, he should bless without the Name and Kingship and meditate on the Name and Kingship in his heart. And one whom sleep overtook in the midst of the morning blessings — any blessing about which he is in doubt whether he recited it, he should not bless out of doubt (and even regarding the blessing of the Torah — he should bless without the Name and Kingship and meditate upon them). And if he forgot and did not recite the morning blessings before prayer, he should recite them after prayer, except for 'HaMachazir Neshamot' (exempted by 'Mechayeh HaMeitim') and the blessing of the Torah (exempted by 'Ahavat Olam').
takeaways: 'Ve'ha'arev' is a second blessing — one answers Amen after the first; and before the blessing of the Torah one may not study (though contemplation is permitted), and women recite it.
One who slept a fixed sleep during the day — it is in doubt whether he must bless again; he should bless without the Name and Kingship and meditate upon them.
One who forgot the morning blessings — he recites them after prayer, except for 'HaMachazir Neshamot' (exempted by 'Mechayeh HaMeitim') and the blessing of the Torah (exempted by 'Ahavat Olam').

paragraphs: Mi sheyyashen ballayla al mittato shinat qeba veneor qodem chatzot lo yebarek birkot hashshachar, ken nireh missetimut dibre hamqubbalim veken nireh middibre zohar haqqadosh bereshit dap yo"d ammud b' veayyen "miqdash melek" sham. ak birkat hattora yukal lebarek qodem chatzot meachar shekkebar yashan shinat qeba vekannireh mizzohar haqqadosh sham veayyen acharonim za"l, mihu im hu neor qarob lachatzot nakon lehamtin ad achar chatzot kede lebarek birkot hashshachar im birkot hattora keseder hattiqqun bekol yom veyihyu qesher echad, veim yirtzeh bizman muat zeh debene ubene yomar pesuqim shel shirot vetishbachot, veshaalti lididenu harab haggaon hechasid morenu harab eliyyahu minni natreh rachamana uparqeh al minhag hachasidim beir haqqodesh tibbaneh vetikkonen bimhera beyamenu veheshib vezeh leshono ben happashtanim ben hamqubbalim kulle alema modo sheim yashan shinat qeba chayyab lebarek veyakol lebarek vekannireh milleshon zohar haqqadosh cheleq ' dap yu"d ammud b' veayyen "miqdash melek", amenam yesh shette kavvanot bebirkat hattora achat peratit vehi hannizkeret b"nahar shalem" dap tz"b ammud ' vezo shayeka gam qodem chatzot, veachat kelalit biklal hy"ch berakot vehi hannizkeret beshaar hakkavvanot depus yerushalayim dap ' ammud g'. veayyen "nehar shalom" dap t"l ammud b' vedap p"z ammud b' beuram, ubevadday hambarek qodem chatzot lo yetaqqen zeh hattiqqun, kevan shehaelyonim lo nitqenu heak yetuqqenu hattachtonim, umikkol maqom hamminhag bebet el ykb"tz bizman shehu qarob lachatzot yesh mebarekin birkat hattora velomedim, ubachatzot yebareku shear habberakot, veyesh chasidim sheap al pi ken mamtinim ad chatzot baabur tiqqun seder hy"ch berakot ad kan leshono natreh rachamana uparqeh:

clarification.explanation: One who slept a fixed sleep at night and awoke before midnight should not recite the morning blessings (as follows from the unqualified words of the Kabbalists and from the Zohar), but he may recite the blessing of the Torah already, since the sleep itself is considered an interruption justifying the blessing. One who awakens close to midnight — it is proper that he wait until after midnight and recite all the blessings (morning and Torah) together, in the fixed daily order, so that they be joined as one; and in the brief interim while he waits, it is good to recite verses of song and praise. And the inner reason for the distinction regarding the blessing of the Torah: Rabbi Eliyahu Mani explains that there are two different intentions within the blessing of the Torah — one 'particular' (relating to the person himself), which applies and is effective even before midnight; and the second 'general,' relating to the overall repair of the order of the eighteen blessings (as alluded to in the Kabbalistic intentions), which is attained only after midnight — because 'the supernal ones have not yet been repaired' at that hour (the repair above is not yet complete), and consequently those below (the blessing here below) cannot complete it beforehand either. For this reason, in Beit El (the fellowship of Kabbalists in Jerusalem) the custom was: one who awakens close to midnight recites the blessing of the Torah and studies Torah already before midnight (since thereby he achieves the particular intention), and waits specifically until midnight for the other blessings; and there are some of the pious who are stringent and wait until midnight even for the blessing of the Torah itself, in order to merit also the complete general repair.
takeaways: One who slept a fixed sleep and awoke before midnight: he should not recite the morning blessings, but he may recite the blessing of the Torah.
Close to midnight — it is preferable to wait and recite all the blessings together after midnight, in the fixed order.

The Kabbalistic reason: the blessing of the Torah has a particular intention (effective even before midnight) and a general intention relating to the overall repair of the eighteen blessings (attained only after midnight).

In Beit El the custom was to recite the blessing of the Torah before midnight and study, and to wait until midnight for the other blessings; and some wait until midnight even for the blessing of the Torah.

paragraphs: Chayyab haadam lebarek mea berakot bekol yom, ubeshabbat veyom tob yachserun mechamat birkot haamida veaz yasim otam bemine perot verecha tob, vehinneh meporash bedibre rabbenu za"l beshaar rucha haqqodesh dap d' ammud ' vezeh leshono "da ki k"b otiyyot lp" byt" hem teluyot bemea berakot shehaadam mebarek bekol yom, vekaasher en haadam mebarek kelal ezo beraka mehem techsar mimmennu otah haot sheotah beraka teluya bah, veim berak ot ella shettaa bah az tihyeh haot hahi metzuya amenam tihyeh chasera beatzmah, veim berak otah ketiqqunah ella shello nitkavven bah az tihyeh haot hahi chashuka ubilti meira" ad kan leshono, umizzeh tabin kamma tzarik haadam lehishtaddel bemea berakot:

clarification.explanation: A person is obligated to recite one hundred blessings every day (on Shabbat/Yom Tov, what is lacking from the Amidah is made up with fruits and pleasant fragrance). According to the secret, the twenty-two letters of the alphabet are dependent upon the hundred daily blessings: a blessing not recited at all — its corresponding letter is lacking; a blessing recited in error — the letter is present but flawed; a blessing recited correctly but without intention — the letter is present but dark and unilluminated.
takeaways: Each of the hundred daily blessings is connected to a letter of the alphabet; precision and intention in the blessing affect the state of that letter (whole/flawed/dark).

paragraphs: Matzati katub tob shehaadam yargil atzmo lomar bekol yom shelosh pesuqim ellu ketubim bedibre hayyamim ' siman k"t "vibarek david et Adonai leene kol haqqahal, veyomar david baruk atta Adonai veku', leka Adonai haggedulla vehaggebura veku' vehaosher vehakkabod millepaneka veku'" vekaasher tiqqenum chakamenu za"l bizmirot bekol yom, vehaadam yomar otam bipne atzmam bekol yom asar o sheba peamim, ubekol paam yomar acharehem pasuq "baruk atta Adonai lammedeni chuqqeka" umillebad toelet sodit sheyyesh baamiratam od toil lo lehashlim lo mispar mea berakot bishat haddechaq ad kan matzati, venireh li shehu minhag yapeh venakon veayyen "pitche teshuba" yoreh dea siman shk"ch seip qatan ' mah shekkatab beshem harab "peri tebua" mah sheqqibbel merabbotayv yeuyyan sham od matzati katub b"keter malkut" ketibat yad minhag yapeh lomar haadam bekol yom pasuq "baruk Adonai leolam amen veamen" (tehillim pt, ng) chamishsha vearbaim peamim, ubeamero amen veamen yekavven beshem hashshillub shel hvy"h dn"y, vezeh happasuq yoil lo bimqom tishim ummanim shechayyab adam lomar bekol yom beet shehu anus veeno yakol laanot kegon shehu yosheb babbayit lebaddo veen holek lebet hakkeneset mechamat ones ad kan. venireh li deminhag yapeh hu zeh, veken ani nahagti lomar pasuq zeh kammispar hannizkar bekol yom achar parasha shel birkat kohanim sheanachnu omerim achar birkat hashshachar bekol yom, veasiti ken kede shello tishshakach amiratam mimmenni meachar sheasiti lah zeman qabua, veachar pasuq zeh ani omer tv"b peamim pasuq "or zarua latztzaddiq" (tehillim tzad, y) kemo shekkatab harab haggaon rabbenu chayyim palagi'y za"l denakon leomero tv"b peamim bekol yom:

clarification.explanation: The Ben Ish Chai found it written that it is fitting to accustom oneself to say every day these three verses (1 Chronicles 29): 'And David blessed the Lord before all the assembly... Yours, O Lord, is the greatness and the power... and the riches and the honor come from You...' — as our Sages instituted them within the Zemirot — and to say them by themselves ten or seven times, and each time afterward 'Baruch Atah Hashem, lamdeini chukecha'; and besides the mystical benefit, this also helps to complete the hundred blessings in a time of pressing need. He also found it written in Keter Malchut a fine custom, to say every day the verse 'Baruch Hashem le'olam, amen ve'amen' forty-five times, having intention at 'amen ve'amen' with the combined Name Havayah-Adonai; and this verse benefits in place of the ninety 'amens' a person is obligated to say every day, when he is prevented by circumstance and unable to answer (such as one sitting alone at home who does not go to the synagogue due to circumstances beyond his control). And the Ben Ish Chai likewise practiced saying it forty-five times every day after the Priestly Blessing recited after the morning blessings (at a fixed time, so as not to forget), and afterward says 'Or zarua latzaddik' seventeen times (following the view of Rabbi Chaim Palaggi).
takeaways: A fine custom: to say every day the three verses 'Vayevarech David... Lecha Hashem hagedulah...' (7 or 10 times, followed each time by 'lamdeini chukecha') — also to help complete the hundred blessings in a time of pressing need.

'Baruch Hashem le'olam, amen ve'amen' 45 times (with intention on the Name Havayah-Adonai) — benefits in place of the 90 'amens' for one prevented by circumstance; followed by 'Or zarua latzaddik' seventeen times.
